title: DeviceRegister
description: What the app says about itself on `POST /devices`. It travels over HTTP rather than the socket — a device has to exist before it may decide anything, and the handshake already needs to know which device it is — but the payload is one contract in three languages all the same.

installId.description: Identity of the installation, minted by the app on first run and kept in the operating system's secure storage. Never an identifier of the device itself: that one survives an uninstall, which is a privacy problem, and this one does not (D-01).

name.description: What the person will recognise in the approval list.

platform.description: Which operating system. Only Android is exercised in this plan (D-12); the app still builds for iOS.

appVersion.description: Version of the app, for diagnostics and for the deprecation window.

pushToken.description: The provider's token for this installation, when there is one. Absent is normal and not an error: a device with no token still watches sessions, and the app re-sends the token on every renewal (D-13).

locale.description: Language the push goes out in — the one exception to the rule that the backend never translates. Absent falls back to `en`.
